our reading: Kept literal: कण्ठमें धारण करता है / holds in his throat.
alternatives: Learns it by heart (कण्ठस्थ करता है, as the existing Hindi); or wears it written as an amulet at the throat.

issue: The object of धारयेत् (…अभिरक्षितम्) is unstated.
our reading: This hymn (the Rakṣā), guarded by the name of Rāma.

issue: गच्छन्मनोरथान्नश्च: नः can be accusative ('us') or genitive ('our'), and गच्छन् does not say where he goes.
our reading: Protect our desires and us (नः acc., च 'and'); गच्छन् = 'as he goes' (not 'ahead').
alternatives: Protect our desires (नः gen.); 'going ahead of us' from the context of śloka 20. Some texts read गच्छन्मनोरथोऽस्माकं.

issue: पुरुषः पूर्णः: two names or one.
our reading: Two names, as our word sheet lists them: the Supreme Person, the Perfect One.

issue: मनोरमे: locative qualifying रामे, or vocative addressing Pārvatī (मनोरमा).
our reading: Locative: 'in Rāma, who delights the mind' (our word sheet; the existing English).
alternatives: Vocative 'O charming one', a second address to Pārvatī alongside वरानने.

issue: Speaker named although the verse does not name him.
our reading: 'शिवजी कहते हैं — / Śiva says:' added, per style §3 (the speaker changes) and the brief (Śiva to Pārvatī); Pārvatī named in the address.
alternatives: Leave the speaker unnamed and keep only the address (हे सुमुखी! / O fair-faced one).

issue: विश्वामित्रप्रिय (sh5) and विप्रप्रिय (sh26): 'dear to X' or 'to whom X is dear'.
our reading: 'Dear to Viśvāmitra', 'dear to the brāhmaṇas' (tatpuruṣa, as our word sheet).
alternatives: Bahuvrīhi: 'to whom Viśvāmitra / the brāhmaṇas are dear' (the existing Hindi has विप्र-भक्त).

issue: शतकोटिप्रविस्तरम्: the unit of 'a hundred crore' is not stated.
our reading: A hundred crore verses (the traditional Śatakoṭi Rāmāyaṇa).
alternatives: Leave the unit unstated ('a hundred crore in extent'), or read it as 'boundless'.

issue: मधुरं मधुराक्षरम्: what each word qualifies.
our reading: मधुरं adverbial ('sweetly'); मधुराक्षरम् = the sweet syllables Rāma, Rāma.
alternatives: Both qualify Vālmīki the cuckoo ('sweet, of sweet syllables'), as our word sheet glosses मधुराक्षरम्.

issue: सर्वत्र goes with अव्याहताज्ञः or with लभते.
our reading: With लभते: he wins victory and well-being everywhere; his command is unchallenged.
alternatives: His command is unchallenged everywhere (the existing Hindi).
